replacement: 16. I even have good reason to be content. If he has not given me the perfection of being superior to error by the first means I noted above, which depends on clear and evident knowledge of everything I can deliberate about, he has at least left in my power the other means: to hold firmly to the resolution never to judge where the truth is not clearly known to me. For, although I am conscious of the weakness that I cannot keep my mind continually fixed on the same thought, I can nevertheless, by attentive and oft-repeated meditation, impress that resolution so strongly on my memory that I will never fail to recall it when I need it, and in this way I can acquire the habit of not erring.
